title: ChatStream Signalsonic Adapter and Retry Playbook
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Problem statement: application teams report confusion and edge-case bugs when integrating streaming chat completions with event-based handlers (partial chunks, tool-calls, function results, and mid-stream errors). Goal: ship a small, well-documented adapter plus a retry playbook that makes streaming ergonomics predictable for Python SDK users, reduces common integration footguns, and provides clear telemetry hooks for SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a reference adapter (SignalsonicAdapter) that normalizes the raw stream into stable iterator semantics (chunk, event-type, watermark) and exposes a simple interface for handlers.
Document three canonical retry strategies (idempotent-retry, resumable-fast-failover, optimistic-ack) with example code for each and tests.
Add telemetry spans and counters for: stream_open, fragment_received, event_parsed, handler_ack, handler_nack, stream_resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure.
Integrate adapter into SDK examples and a sample reference app in examples/chat-signalsonic/.
Create migration guidance for existing users using the current stream API; include minimal breaking-change surface.

Automated unit and integration tests covering: partial fragment reassembly, duplicate fragment deduplication, mid-stream tool-call extraction, resume after transient network error, and graceful shutdown with checkpointing.
Design review approval and PR merged with biweekly canary rollout to hosted API customers under feature flag.
technical_notes: Adapter will sit between raw SSE/WebSocket stream layer and public Python iterator returned by chat.stream().

Core responsibilities: assemble byte fragments into tokens/fragments, attach monotonic watermarks, synthesize event envelope (type: text_chunk|tool_call|function_result|end), and expose stable sequence IDs for idempotency.

Resume strategy: checkpoint = latest committed sequence_id + KV-cache prefix fingerprint. Resume request sent with resume_after_id and session_token; server-side will support resume with truncated KV cache warnings.

Retries: separate transport-level transient retries from semantic retries. Transport retries attempted automatically up to 3 times with exponential backoff. Semantic retries (replay) require adapter checkpoint to avoid double-execution of side-effecting tools.
Backpressure: adapter exposes an async .ack() hook for handlers to signal safe-to-advance; default behavior uses bounded queue with pluggable low/high watermarks.
Telemetry: use existing SDK tracer naming conventions (sdk.stream.signalsonic.*). Counters should be taggable by model, route, customer_id.
Compatibility: keep public API backward-compatible where possible; provide MigrationCompat shim for users relying on raw event shapes.
Performance budget: adapter must add <1ms median per-fragment overhead on typical 8k context chat on dedicated infra.
design_decisions: Name: SignalsonicAdapter chosen to emphasize event-signal normalization and low-latency semantics.
Expose both sync and async iterator surfaces. Primary recommendation: async iterator for server-driven streaming apps.
Use sequence_id (string) rather than ordinal to support multi-source merge in future (e.g., multi-model fanout).
Provide built-in convenience decorators: @idempotent_handler and @resumable_handler to help users opt into semantics with minimal boilerplate.
Do not attempt automatic dedup across restarts without explicit user checkpointing to avoid side-effect duplication by default.
